title: What can you say about valerian in your ads and on your site?
summary: The library supports 2 wordings for valerian; the strongest is "Traditionally used in herbal medicine to help relieve occasional sleeplessness" (limited, 0.3-12 g dried root (or extract equivalent) a day). Avoid wording that names or implies a disease, a drug or a treatment, such as "Treats insomnia".

supported_wordings.wording: Traditionally used in herbal medicine to help relieve occasional sleeplessness.
supported_wordings.why: Traditional use in Health Canada's monograph; ODS calls the clinical evidence on sleep problems inconclusive.
supported_wordings.daily_dose: 0.3-12 g dried root (or extract equivalent) a day
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older; at most 3.6 g per dose; take 30-60 minutes before bedtime as needed.

supported_wordings.wording: Traditionally used in herbal medicine to help relieve restlessness or nervousness.
supported_wordings.why: Traditional use in Health Canada's monograph; no other listed source supports it.
supported_wordings.daily_dose: 0.3-12 g dried root (or extract equivalent) a day
supported_wordings.dose_details: Adults 18 and older; at most 3.6 g per dose.

wordings_to_avoid.why: Names a sleep disorder; ODS says evidence for valerian in insomnia is inconclusive.
Compares the product to a drug.

wordings_to_avoid.wording: Helps you fall asleep if you have difficulty falling asleep
wordings_to_avoid.why: FDA's 2000 rule (page 1031) says this implies treating insomnia unless the product is clearly for occasional sleeplessness.
FDA's 2000 rule (page 1031) says help falling asleep implies treating insomnia unless the context makes clear the product is only for occasional sleeplessness.

evidence_strengths.strong: At least two listed sources support it independently at a comparable dose and form, and none disagrees.
evidence_strengths.moderate: One listed source supports it as an evidence-based use at that dose, and no listed source disagrees.
evidence_strengths.limited: The only support is traditional use, the sources disagree, or the source itself calls the evidence weak.

reasons_to_avoid.drug: names a drug or presents the product as one
reasons_to_avoid.treatment: promises to treat, cure or prevent a condition

sources.name: FDA final rule on structure/function statements, 65 FR 1000 (6 January 2000), page 1031

disclaimer: Not legal advice. This guide shows the wording that published evidence supports at a daily dose, from the sources linked below; it is not a ruling on any claim. Your own product, its form and dose, and your own evidence still need to match the wording you use.
